subject: EdgeSentinel: new telemetry processor — country scope & export clarification
messages:
From: EdgeSentinel Onboarding <ops@edgesentinel.io>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com, grace.oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: 
Date: Wed, 20 Aug 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Notice: onboarding of CloudTransit as telemetry processor (June->Aug ops)

Hi Olga / Kimberly / Grace,

Quick heads-up from EdgeSentinel: over the next 30 days we will add CloudTransit Inc. as a subprocessor to handle ephemeral telemetry ingestion and enrichment for our edge agents in North America and EU. This change only affects telemetry logs (latency metrics, anonymized host IDs, agent debug traces) used for service health and routing.

Files attached: edgesentinel_subprocessor_roster.csv (fields: name, role, countries, retention, contact) and a short SOC2 pointer.

High-level notes: 
- CloudTransit will receive non-PI telemetry (we've redacted device identifiers at collection) and will store encrypted blobs in their US and EU regions.
- Retention: 45 days by default, 120 days for agreed incidents.
- No customer content or prompt text will be sent to them.

Can you confirm whether we need to provide additional dataflow charts or a DPA addendum for this scope? Happy to hop on a quick call if useful.

Thanks,

Carlos Marin
Onboarding Lead
EdgeSentinel

Attachments: edgesentinel_subprocessor_roster.csv (CSV stub)

From: olga.petrov@redwood.com <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: ops@edgesentinel.io, carlos@edgesentinel.io
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.com, grace.oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 20 Aug 2025 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Notice: onboarding of CloudTransit as telemetry processor (June->Aug ops)

Hi Carlos / EdgeSentinel team — thanks for the notification and roster. A few items we need to confirm before we sign off: 

1) Country scope: the roster lists US and "EU" — please specify which EU member states will host data (we need region-level mapping for our DPA).
2) Data types: you say "non-PI telemetry" — please provide the exact schema or a small sample (anonymized) so our privacy team can validate no user-generated content or prompt traces are included.
3) Encryption & keys: confirm whether CloudTransit will use customer-managed keys or provider-managed KMS, and whether keys are stored in the same jurisdiction as the data.
4) Export & subprocessors: will CloudTransit subcontract any downstream processors (e.g., analytics or S3 replication vendors)? If so, list them and their countries.

Also tagging Kimberly and Grace for procurement/legal review. If you can attach a brief processing map (dataflow) and their SOC2 link, that will speed review. If you prefer a 30-minute call tomorrow, I'm available 2-4pm PT.

Olga Petrov
Senior Privacy Program Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Carlos Marin <carlos@edgesentinel.io>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com, grace.oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: legal@edgesentinel.io
Date: Thu, 21 Aug 2025 08:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Notice: onboarding of CloudTransit as telemetry processor (June->Aug ops)

Hi Olga / Kimberly / Grace — thanks for the rapid reply. Answers below and I attached a simple processing map (processing_map_v1.pdf).

1) Country scope: primary regions are US (us-east-1) and Frankfurt, DE (eu-central-1). No other EU member states are currently used.
2) Data schema: telemetry schema attached — fields are timestamp, agent_id_hash (one-way SHA256), event_type, latency_ms, region, agent_version. No free-text fields, no customer payloads. We redacted agent_id to hashed values only.
3) Keys: CloudTransit uses provider-managed KMS in each region (separate keys in us-east-1 and eu-central-1). They support BYOK but that requires a contract addendum; currently provider-managed.
4) Downstream processors: CloudTransit replicates encrypted telemetry to an archival store run by ArchiveCloud (us-west-2) for failover retention. ArchiveCloud is listed in the attached roster.

SOC2 link: https://docsend.com/view/edgesentinel-soc2-report (short tokenized view).

Let me know if you'd like copies of their data retention/erase playbook — I can request that from CloudTransit. Happy to join a call tomorrow at 3pm PT if helpful.

Best,
Carlos
Onboarding Lead, EdgeSentinel

Attachments: processing_map_v1.pdf, soc2-link.txt

From: kimberly.park@redwood.com <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: ops@edgesentinel.io, carlos@edgesentinel.io
Cc: olga.petrov@redwood.com, grace.oconnor@redwood.com, markus.klein@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 22 Aug 2025 14:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Notice: onboarding of CloudTransit as telemetry processor (June->Aug ops)

Hi Carlos / EdgeSentinel legal — appreciate the details and the processing map. A couple of legal/procurement asks before we can accept CloudTransit as a subprocessor under our DPA: 

- DPA addendum: please confirm CloudTransit will sign the standard subprocessor DPA addendum (I can share our template). We specifically need commitments on: encryption at rest, prompt/PI exclusion clause, cooperation for data subject requests, and onshore fallback notice.
- BYOK path: if CloudTransit can support BYOK within 30 days we can mark this as low risk; otherwise we need a compensating control (e.g., restricted retention and additional audit rights).
- ArchiveCloud: list the export boundaries used for the archival copy and provide ArchiveCloud's SOC2 link.
- Evidence package: please provide CloudTransit's data deletion playbook and a contact for urgent breach notifications.

Olga / Grace — please advise if privacy requires any additional items beyond the schema and processing map. Markus, tagging you for a brief legal review; if you want, I'll send a redline DPA addendum draft to ops@edgesentinel.io and legal@edgesentinel.io.

Thanks,

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Contracts
Redwood Inference
